concretechanges.before: Death is not an event. It is a border condition. Every state transition requires a surrender of the old configuration before the new one appears.
concretechanges.after: The border in this essay is a way of reading change: an old configuration can become unlivable before another is available.

concretechanges.before: The Vedic tradition encodes this same operation as Nigredo: the calcination that reduces the dross of inherited assumptions to ash before new architecture can be installed.
concretechanges.after: I borrow Nigredo from alchemical imagery for this stripping away of inherited assumptions; the connection is made here, rather than inherited from Vedic teaching.

concretechanges.before: The Vedic Kṣaṇika-vāda tradition holds that all conditioned phenomena are momentary. Each phenomenon arises, persists for a single kṣaṇa, and ceases. Nothing endures from one moment to the next. What appears as continuity is a succession of discrete events, each one dying into its successor. That is literal, not figurative. The kṣaṇa names a real structural limit: the smallest duration in which a state can persist before it must surrender.
concretechanges.after: Buddhist discussions of momentariness offer a philosophical neighbour to this image. I draw on the question they raise about apparent continuity; I am not treating a kṣaṇa as a measured minimum duration in physics.

concretechanges.before: It enters a temporary suspension, a neural apoptosis where the old pattern stops executing without being erased.
concretechanges.after: “Neural apoptosis” would confuse cell death with altered experience. The comparison here concerns a loosened self-story, not deletion of neurons.

concretechanges.before: The Vedic tradition calls this *anutpāda* — non-arising, the recognition that nothing is born and nothing dies because nothing persists long enough to be either. The border is not a place. It is a duration measured in the smallest unit of causal time.
concretechanges.after: The border image helps me describe the interval without making it a unit of causal time. A philosophical account of non-arising and a report of altered experience require different kinds of interpretation.

concretechanges.before: At the cosmic scale, a star's death seeds the elements that form new worlds. The supernova is not destruction. It is the nucleosynthesis of everything heavier than iron. The carbon in your bones, the calcium in your teeth, the iron in your blood — all forged in stellar furnaces that reached their structural limit and surrendered. The pattern nests. The personal is the systemic is the cosmic.
concretechanges.after: Stellar ash gives the essay another image of material surviving the form that held it. Its appeal does not establish that a collapsing star and a changing self follow one mechanism.

concretechanges.before: In consciousness, this is the rigid self-model that refuses decoupling — the DMN that will not let go, looping the same autobiographical narrative until the neural substrate degrades.
concretechanges.after: A rigid self-story offers a metaphorical comparison; it is not a diagnosis of a default mode network or an explanation of neural degradation.

concretechanges.before: At the personal scale, this is the interval between breaths where the old self stops and the next has not yet begun. At the interpersonal scale, this is the rupture in a relationship where old patterns are recognized as unviable. At the systemic scale, this is the institutional collapse that clears space for new structures. At the cosmic scale, this is the heat death of a star seeding the elements that will form new worlds. The pattern nests. The personal is the systemic is the cosmic. The Kha-Ba-La triad operates at every scale: Kha is the observer who sees the border; Ba is the substrate that must cross it; La is the resistance that makes the crossing real.
concretechanges.after: A relationship can reach a point where its familiar terms no longer work. The border image then asks something uncomfortable: which papers are we still presenting after their authority has expired? Kha, Ba and La are my vocabulary for the noticing, embodied consequence and resistance involved in that question.

concretechanges.before: Card XIII does not show a grim reaper. It shows a border guard. The skeletal figure holds a passport stamp, not a scythe.
concretechanges.after: In the card I imagine for this essay, XIII becomes a border guard. The skeletal figure holds a passport stamp rather than a scythe.

concretechanges.before: The system succeeds when the user no longer needs the border — when every configuration is recognized as temporary, every state as a kṣaṇa, and the observer watches the succession without clinging to any single frame. The Quine is complete when the traveler no longer needs a passport. The Nigredo is complete when the ash is no longer mourned but recognized as the starting material for every form that ever was.
concretechanges.after: The passport image leaves a harder question than a promise of completion: what will I carry across, and what am I still trying to prove with expired papers?

concretechanges.before: That is literal, not figurative. The kṣaṇa names a real structural limit: the smallest duration in which a state can persist before it must surrender.
concretechanges.after: The philosophical claim is stronger than a loose image of change. It still does not supply a minimum duration measured by physics.

concretechanges.before: Every cellular exchange, every neural firing, every ionic current across the fascial network is a discrete transaction.
concretechanges.after: Cellular exchange and neural firing give me contemporary images of events; they do not verify that philosophical account.

concretechanges.before: The observer sees the border. The body is the substrate that must cross it. The resistance is the friction that makes the crossing meaningful. Without the observer, the crossing is blind — you are reshuffled without awareness. Without the body, the crossing is abstract — philosophy without somatic consequence. Without the resistance, the crossing is frictionless — and frictionless change is not change; it is dissipation. The three co-arise, or nothing arises.
concretechanges.after: At a border, noticing the expired papers does not carry a body across. Something has to move, and something resists. The passport image keeps that difficulty visible.
